desc:
Given an integer array nums (any order) and an integer target, count the triples of positions i < j < k with nums[i] + nums[j] + nums[k] < target.

nums = [-2, 0, 1, 3], target = 2
valid triples: (-2,0,1) and (-2,0,3)
result = 2

The triples are counted by position, so repeated values produce separate triples.
hints: Enumerating all triples is O(n³). The condition only depends on the values, not on their order.
Sort the array and fix the smallest element of the triple by index. Now count the pairs after it whose sum is below target - a[i].
For the pair part, use lo and hi: if a[i] + a[lo] + a[hi] < target, then a[lo] works with every index in lo+1..hi, which adds hi - lo triples at once.
editorial: After sorting, every triple of positions maps to a triple of sorted positions with the same values, so counting sorted triples i < lo < hi is enough. For a fixed i, let lo = i + 1, hi = n - 1. If the sum is below the target, all middle indices lo+1..hi are at most a[hi], so the pairs (lo, lo+1), ..., (lo, hi) all qualify: add hi - lo and advance lo. Otherwise decrease hi.

The inner sweep is linear, so the total is O(n²) after the sort. This is the “count under a bound” version of 3Sum: because we only need a number, we can add whole ranges at once instead of listing triples, and duplicates need no special handling.
